status: editorial wording only; no new scientific review or evidence
basis: Unchanged eCLIP C_R6 and scATAC R13.atac_assay analyses; these claims were also accepted in focused review job52178921. Original scientific records remain available.

text.before: iCLIP uses UV-C crosslinking, partial RNA digestion and antibody capture of the selected RNA-binding protein. Gel electrophoresis and membrane transfer precede proteinase K recovery of the attached RNA.
text.after: eCLIP retains this capture and purification route. The recovered RNA then enters its modified library-conversion procedure.

text.compared_feature: eCLIP replaces cDNA circularization with direct adapter ligation
text.before: iCLIP ligates an RNA 3′ adapter and reverse transcribes the RNA with a primer carrying inverse adapter regions and a BamHI site. The cDNA is circularized and reopened with BamHI to make it amplifiable.
text.after: eCLIP ligates an indexed 3′ adapter to bead-bound RNA, reverse transcribes the RNA, then ligates a second ssDNA adapter directly to the cDNA 3′ end. Direct adapter ligation replaces circularization and BamHI reopening while preserving the crosslink-proximal reverse-transcription endpoint.
effect_descriptions: In matched RBFOX2 experiments, the normalized PCR estimate implies approximately 1,000-fold more pre-amplification adapter-ligated material for eCLIP than the locally generated iCLIP library, assuming 100% PCR efficiency.
At matched uniquely mapped read depth, eCLIP produced a higher usable-read fraction than the local RBFOX2 iCLIP experiment.
eCLIP retained the crosslink-associated read-termination pattern seen with local iCLIP and previously reported RBFOX2 motif positions.
scope_notes: The result baseline is the local RBFOX2 iCLIP experiment; the procedure comparison above describes the original HeLa hnRNP C iCLIP implementation.
The eCT estimate assumes 100% PCR efficiency. Random-mer sequencing errors can inflate apparent molecule counts near saturation.
The exact local iCLIP variant and reagent differences remain unspecified in the registered material; the supplementary protocol and comparator figures were not separately available.

text.compared_feature: eCLIP moves molecular tags from the RT primer to the cDNA adapter
text.before: Original iCLIP carries a three-base random molecular tag in its reverse-transcription primer. Reads sharing the genomic truncation nucleotide and tag are treated as PCR copies.
text.after: eCLIP installs an N5 or N10 random tag in the ssDNA adapter ligated after reverse transcription. Duplicate reads share the Read1 start, Read2 start and random-mer sequence.
scope_notes: Random-mer sequencing errors can inflate apparent unique-molecule counts near saturation.
The registered main text specifies endpoint-and-tag matching but does not specify an adopted barcode error-correction algorithm.

text.compared_feature: Microfluidic scATAC-seq assigns accessibility libraries to individual cells
text.before: ATAC-seq tags accessible chromatin in pooled preparations of unfixed nuclei and amplifies one population library. Its low-input 500- and 5,000-nucleus variants transfer the transposition reaction directly into PCR.
text.after: Microfluidic scATAC-seq captures individual cells on the Fluidigm C1 IFC and performs transposition and initial PCR on-chip. Recovered cell-origin libraries receive cell-identifying PCR indexes before pooling and sequencing.
effect_descriptions: scATAC-seq was reported to improve input sensitivity by more than 500-fold relative to the published ATAC-seq benchmark that profiled down to 500 nuclei.
Quality-filtered C1 chambers yielded an average of 7.3×10⁴ fragments mapping to the nuclear genome.
scope_notes: The fragment yield applies to chambers passing quality filters; low-diversity and poor-accessibility chambers were excluded.
Single-cell coverage is sparse: about 9.4% of promoters were represented in a typical library, limiting analysis of variation at individual elements.
The earlier ATAC-seq study reported diminished sensitivity at smaller inputs.
Exact lysis, end-processing, indexing and final-purification details remain unresolved because the supplementary Methods/Discussion and oligonucleotide table were not separately available.

text.compared_feature: Microfluidic scATAC-seq optimizes Tn5 release before downstream processing
text.before: Standard 50,000-cell ATAC-seq purifies transposed DNA before PCR. The earlier 500- and 5,000-cell variants already omit that purification.
text.after: Microfluidic scATAC-seq introduces Tn5 release between transposition and downstream amplification so enzymatic processing can continue without DNA purification.
effect_descriptions: Release-optimization conditions increased qPCR-measured library diversity relative to no-release and MinElute-purification controls.
Releasing Tn5 from DNA was intended to permit downstream enzymatic reactions without DNA purification.
scope_notes: The final on-chip release reagent and condition-specific fold gains require the unavailable supplementary Methods and condition table.
EDTA and SDS were tested for in-vitro Tn5–DNA dissociation; the adopted on-chip condition remains unspecified.
A preceding method for this release design is not identified in the available sources.
